subject: RE: Request for UK SOC 2 evidence, KMS residency & bridge letter
messages:
From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finservbank.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finservbank.com
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request for UK SOC 2 evidence, KMS residency & bridge letter

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed. Procurement and InfoSec have a few follow-ups as we move toward contract review. Can you help with the following items so we can complete our due diligence?

1) SOC 2 Type II: We need the current report for the audit period that includes Mar 1 - Apr 30, 2026. If you don't have exact overlap with our required window, can you provide a bridge letter that confirms continuous controls coverage and the next available audit window?

2) Hosting / data residency: Please confirm where TLS termination and persistent storage for the UK region are located for the hosted offering. We need to verify whether keys and disk encryption can be scoped to UK-only infrastructure.

3) Key management: Are customer data encryption keys (KMS) managed in a UK region option or always in a US KMS? If you support customer-managed keys in a British HSM/KMS, please clarify the model and any operational limitations.

4) Evidence samples: Could you share: a) an anonymized access log sample showing principal, timestamp, and region; b) the network diagram for the UK hosting footprint; and c) evidence of logging retention/archival policies?

5) SIG / CAIQ: We will be running SIG-Lite and CAIQ on our side. Do you have a current SIG-Lite export or CAIQ answers you can share to accelerate the review?

We aim to finish InfoSec review by June 4. Please let me know what you can share and approximate delivery dates.

Thanks,
Olivia Turner
Senior InfoSec Manager, FinServ Bank
+44 20 7000 4000

--
FinServ Bank
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finservbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: Request for UK SOC 2 evidence, KMS residency & bridge letter

Hi Olivia — great to hear from you and glad the demo resonated. Looping in Marissa (Customer Security) and Karthik (Legal/Contracts) to help us coordinate the deliverables. Answers inline and next steps below.

1) SOC 2 Type II: We can share the latest SOC 2 Type II report covering the period 2025-07-01 to 2026-04-30. We understand your audit window partially overlaps; we can provide a brief bridge letter that attests controls continuity for 2026-05-01 through 2026-06-30 and confirm our next audit start date. Will that cover your procurement requirement or do you need a different granularity?

2) Hosting / data residency: For our Hosted (public) offering, TLS termination occurs in the region where the customer routes traffic (we currently support UK and EU regions in our hosted fleet). Persistent storage for instances pinned to the UK region resides in UK zones (managed volumes in our UK cloud region). We will provide the network/infra diagram for the UK footprint.

3) Key management: We offer two models: 
  - Redwood-managed KMS with keys stored in the UK region (default for customers who select UK residency).
  - Customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) via customer KMS federation — this requires a dedicated Private deployment or Dedicated with KMS peering; there are some contractual and onboarding steps. We'll include a short note on operational differences.

4) Evidence samples: Attached are: redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf (summary + redaction-friendly SOC2 statement), redwood_network_diagram_uk_region.png, and sample_access_log_excerpt.txt (anonymized). We will also attach our logging retention policy snippet.

5) SIG / CAIQ: Attached is a SIG-lite export (SIG-lite-responses.xlsx). For CAIQ we usually provide a populated questionnaire on request; we can push a CAIQ export to your secure drive link if you'd like.

Next steps:
- Marissa will prepare the bridge letter draft for legal review (target delivery Tue 2026-05-26).
- Karthik will review any contractual language you need for KMS residency and customer-managed key clauses.
- I'll upload a CAIQ export to your shared Drive link if you confirm the best place.

If you need anything sooner, flag the specific items and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Ava Chen
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf; redwood_network_diagram_uk_region.png; sample_access_log_excerpt.txt; SIG-lite-responses.xlsx
From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finservbank.com>

Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 08:36:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Request for UK SOC 2 evidence, KMS residency & bridge letter

Thanks Ava — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple of clarification points from InfoSec and Procurement: 

- The SOC 2 Type II summary is helpful; however we will still need the full report under NDA. Can the full report be shared under a one-way NDA (we can use our standard confidentiality addendum)?

- For the bridge letter, can you confirm the precise dates covered (we need an unambiguous start/end) and whether it will be signed by your external auditor or an authorized Redwood officer?

- KMS: Procurement wants language that keys and key material will not be exported outside the UK if we choose UK-region Redwood-managed KMS. If you support this, we will ask Legal to add a clause; otherwise we need to understand fallbacks.

- Logs: the sample looks good; are logs shipped to a UK cloud region for customers who opt into UK residency? Also what is the default retention period and can that be configured to match our 90/365 day tiers?

If you can confirm those four points and drop the full SOC 2 under NDA, Procurement will move to redlines. Timing is still June 4 for our completion goal.

Best,
Olivia
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Request for UK SOC 2 evidence, KMS residency & bridge letter

Hi Olivia — Marissa here from Customer Security. Quick answers and concrete next steps below.

1) Full SOC 2 report under NDA: we are happy to share the full Type II report under a one-way NDA. I'll send the NDA template in a separate email and, once executed, we will provide a secure PDF copy.

2) Bridge letter: draft attached (redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf includes a bridge paragraph). The draft bridge letter coverage we propose: 2026-05-01 through 2026-06-30. It will be signed by an authorized Redwood officer and countersigned by our external auditor where they provide a concurrence statement. We'll mark signature blocks clearly. If you need the bridge to extend to 2026-07-15 to align with your procurement window, tell us and we can extend the end date.

3) KMS residency: For customers selecting UK-region Redwood-managed KMS, key material and backups remain in UK-region KMS and are not exported outside the UK as part of normal operations. The exception would be customer-initiated replication to other regions — that requires explicit consent and configuration. For customer-managed keys, we will document peering/federation limitations in the SOW. We can add a contractual clause to ensure material is not exported without written approval.

4) Logs & retention: Access logs for UK-resident workloads are stored in the UK region by default when UK residency is selected. Default retention is 90 days for raw access logs and 365 days for aggregated audit events; both can be adjusted via request for Dedicated/Private customers and through our retention policy process for Hosted customers. We'll provide the retention configuration options in the SOW appendix.

Deliverables and timing:
- NDA for SOC 2 report: I will email our standard one-way NDA today (Tue 2026-05-26).
- Bridge letter draft (in summary PDF): attached. If you confirm end date by EOD Wed 2026-05-27 we will finalize signatures by Fri 2026-05-29.
- Full SOC 2 PDF: delivery within 24 hours of NDA execution.
- CAIQ export: we can upload to your Drive link by Wed 2026-05-27 if you confirm the location.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through any evidence items.

Thanks — we want to make the procurement path smooth.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Security, Redwood Inference
